S30 — Settings · Distribution

The Distribution tab of Settings (doc 13 §6.5, doc 15): connect status per client (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Cline), per-target managed-block configuration (the marker-bounded block written into each tool's native session-context file, doc 15 §3.2), the inject content policy and token budget (what gets injected and under what config-row budget, doc 15 §3.4), the curb control (the human sees and curbs push — never a silent context swap, doc 01 F10), the inject log (the durable event_type=inject record, doc 15 §7), the render watermark (a config row, not a table, doc 04 §7), and labels-survive-injection visibility — a corroborated fact is pushed into a tool's context still labelled corroborated, a superseded memory still labelled superseded. Almost everything this board renders is target-new (doc 15 §1's scaffolding-honesty note): the pull door (memory_search over /mcp) exists today, but DistributionService, auto-inject, and the managed-block writer are all target work.

Distribution — empty (no clients connected)

Honesty rule: empty says why, and offers the fix. A fresh install has run no onboarding command yet, so no client's MCP config has been written and no push has ever fired — the empty state names that cause and surfaces the exact one-command fix (doc 15 §5) rather than a bare blank.
Distribution 0 clients connected empty
No clients connected darkmem has not been wired into any agent tool yet — no .mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, ~/.codex/config.toml, or Cline MCP settings entry points here. Connect one to start pulling context via MCP tools and, optionally, pushing an auto-injected managed block.

Distribution — loading

Loading skeletons mirror the exact icon / name / status-chip / meta slots the populated client rows below fill in, so the board never jumps once the connect-status and inject-log reads resolve (doc 14 §5).
Distribution loading

Distribution — error

Honesty rule: error ≠ empty list. When the render-watermark config rows or the events read behind the inject log fails, the board raises a named error rather than returning zero rows indistinguishable from the genuine no-clients empty state (invariant 14) — retry stays offered, and each connected client's own push keeps running server-side even while this board cannot display it (the same "the mechanism is unaffected by the display failing" framing S21 uses for the job registry).
Distribution error
Couldn't load distribution state — the config/events read failed The distribution:watermark:* config rows and the inject/inject_curbed events rows could not be read. This is a display failure only: a client whose push was already active keeps injecting on its own session-start cadence, and a curb already in effect stays in effect — neither is controlled by this board's own uptime. Retry

Distribution — populated (hero, both themes)

Four clients from doc 15 §3.3's adapter registry (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Cline) — three connected and pushing, one curbed (Codex CLI: connected, but the human turned push off), one not yet connected (Cline, its onboarding CTA shown inline — a per-row state distinct from the whole-board empty above, which requires zero clients). Every module the brief names is represented: connect status per client, per-target managed-block config, the inject content policy and token budget, the curb control, the populated inject log, the render watermark, and a dedicated labels-survive-injection panel.

# Project notes (the human's own rules — never touched) <!-- darkmem:begin --> # generated 2026-07-24T14:12:03Z, project darkmem, 8 items, 1,840/2,000 tokens - [L2 · corroborated] hybrid_search_enabled is on by default; RRF k=60 - [L2 · corroborated] confidence_rank_gamma defaults to 0 — inactive until raised - [L0 · summary] pipeline Phase 5 writes vector + graph in two savepoints … 5 more, truth-first order, top-K under the token budget <!-- darkmem:end -->
Only the bytes between the two markers change on refresh (strip-before-rewrite, doc 15 §3.2); the human's own content above the block is never touched.

Inject content policy & token budget

L2 · fact → L3 · article → L0 · summary → fill truth-first until the budget is spent, then stop (top-K, stated in the block header — not silent degradation)
inject_token_budget 2,000 tokens config row, per-target tunable — Codex CLI overrides to 1,200 below
refresh cadence session-start one F3 read + one idempotent write per session; watch mode is a deferred, config-gated Phase-4 enhancement
cold-start fallback candidates, labelled served only when nothing corroborated/confirmed fits the budget yet
codex-cli override inject_token_budget = 1,200 tokens a smaller per-target budget, tuned for AGENTS.md's terser convention — the adapter registry and the budget are both config rows, never hard-coded (convention 9)

Inject log — which inject happened where

claude-code event_type inject · project darkmem · 8 items 2026-07-24 14:12:03 UTC 1,840/2,000 tok
cursor event_type inject · project darkmem · 6 items 2026-07-24 14:10:41 UTC 1,510/2,000 tok
codex-cli event_type inject_curbed · push disabled by operator q.tran 2026-07-24 13:58:12 UTC block → empty markers
codex-cli event_type inject · project darkmem · 5 items (last delivery before the curb above) 2026-07-24 13:40:02 UTC 960/1,200 tok
inject_curbed is a target-new addition to doc 04 §8.1's closed event_type vocabulary — edited into the taxonomy before any code writes it, never bypassed with a free-form value (doc 15 §7). Each row records that the server selected and returned N items for a target; it is not a receipt that the client's file was actually written — an honest limit of the pull-then-write model, stated rather than implied away.

Labels survive injection — expanding the 14:12 UTC claude-code delivery

asserted by 3 distinct origins of kinds [code, memory], no known contradiction, as of 2026-07-20 — hybrid_search_enabled is on by default; RRF k=60
L0 · memory superseded injected as: superseded, amber, lineage-requested
"the reranker was skipped by default" — superseded_by → memory 7a1c4e0, kept only because this session's declared context asked for supersession lineage on retrieval ranking
Neither item is relabelled on the way into the tool: a corroborated fact keeps its full badge claim, and a superseded memory keeps its amber lifecycle label rather than being silently promoted to active or dropped (doc 13 §6.5, doc 15 §3.4, invariant 14). The .badge/.layer-chip markup here is composed verbatim from C01/C02, not re-derived.

S31 — Auth: Login, populated (hero, both themes)

Scope of this fragment. Realises doc 13 §2/§3's _guest layout route (/login) — the atmospheric glass card centred over the particle/aurora backdrop (doc 14 §2: "the login/setup flow's glass card over the interactive particle/aurora backdrop ... is the language's ceremonial register, reserved for the unauthenticated threshold surfaces"). The form mirrors the shipped login-card.tsx/login-form.tsx exactly: darkmem is single-admin, trust-on-first-use (doc 18 §3) — one password field, no username, because there is exactly one account to authenticate against. States: 4 boards — populated (this one, hero in both themes) / loading / error / rate-limited lockout.
Static still-frame — motion out of scope. The live component (particle-background.tsx) drifts particles continuously, links nearby nodes, and repels/links toward the cursor when interactive; it degrades to fewer particles with no cursor interaction on touch/low-core devices, and to exactly this kind of single frozen frame under prefers-reduced-motion (doc 14 §7 lists "the existing particle backdrop on the threshold surfaces" as one of the app's few closed motion-as-signal uses). This board renders that reduced-motion frame permanently — no canvas, no animation loop, no cursor listeners.
Token-derived, not hardcoded (mockup contract). The shipped component today hardcodes its palette (#818cf8, #22d3ee, ...). This board instead derives every backdrop colour from --primary / --chart-1 / --chart-5 / --info so the atmosphere already re-themes with an accent change — the same migration doc 14 §2's "no hardcoded hex in app components, ever" rule implies for the component itself, not yet done in frontend/src.

S31 — Auth: Login, rate-limited lockout

Per-IP lockout, honestly named as a distinct state, not another "invalid password" (doc 18 §3). Login rate limiting is per-IP with lockout — the client IP comes from X-Real-IP under a trusted proxy, never the spoofable leftmost X-Forwarded-For. The shipped LoginRateLimiter defaults (backend/app/services/login_rate_limit.py) are 5 failed attempts inside a 300-second window before a 5-minute lockout; a locked IP gets 429 with detail: "Too many failed login attempts; retry in {n}s" and a Retry-After header, checked before the DB is touched or any password hashed. Doc 18 §3 marks these thresholds target-new to move from code constants into tunable config rows, and lockouts as journaling to events (auth_lockout, also target-new) — today each failed attempt already writes an auth_login_failed audit row.

S32 — Auth: trust-on-first-use setup wizard

The _guest-layout counterpart to S31's login board (doc 13 §2/§3): a four-step wizard — password → LLM → repo path → finish — served at /setup and gated end-to-end by require_uninitialized. Every wizard endpoint (including the two filesystem-browse endpoints step 3 uses) 403s the moment the admin_password_hash config row exists (doc 18 §3): the first party to finish the wizard on a fresh box owns it, and there is no pre-shared SETUP_SECRET to reintroduce — that secret-distribution problem was judged strictly worse than the bounded TOFU race it would close. The board renders the ceremonial register doc 14 §2 reserves for unauthenticated threshold surfaces — a glass card over a static stand-in for the particle/ aurora backdrop — matching S31's register rather than the app's calm instrumental default.

S32 — step 1 of 4: admin password (hero, both themes)

Trust-on-first-use, not a shared secret. /api/v1/setup/* is gated only by require_uninitialized; there is no pre-shared setup key to distribute before the box has an owner. The password the visitor sets here is the claim — whoever completes this step first owns the box, and the wizard closes to every later visitor (S32-error below). Rendered as the hero in both themes; the remaining three steps and the loading/error states render once, in the default theme, since the shared toggle in mockup.css/theme.css already guarantees theme parity.

S32 — state: loading (finalizing)

Honesty rule: a submitted draft is not a completed setup until its own block reports back. POST /api/v1/setup is not one atomic write — the password block commits immediately and unconditionally (a stale connection afterward can never lose the admin account); the LLM and repo blocks each run in their own savepoint and each report their own {ok, message}. Back and Skip disable for the whole in-flight window rather than allowing a step change mid-submit.

S32 — state: error (setup window already closed)

Honesty rule: the TOFU race is named, never disguised as a generic failure. Every /api/v1/setup/* call — including this one — 403s the instant the admin_password_hash config row exists (doc 18 §3's "setup takeover" row): the LAN boundary plus the minutes between first boot and wizard completion bound the race window, and once someone closes it the wizard has nothing left to offer a later visitor except a pointer to /login. This is not a network/server error — the request succeeded and was correctly refused.
